description: PyAEZ is the Asian Institute of Technology Geoinformatics Center's Python implementation of agro-ecological zoning calculations, developed with FAO support. It combines climate assessment, crop biomass and yield calculations, water limitation, soil and terrain constraints, and economic suitability. Users supply climate series, crop parameters, soil properties and terrain inputs, including documented spreadsheet lookup tables; outputs include crop suitability and yield estimates. Geographic coverage and spatial detail follow the supplied grids and parameters. Public source, examples and documentation are free under MIT. A limitation is that local parameter quality and assumptions determine suitability results; the repository describes some soil-layer functionality as experimental and distinguishes accelerated calculations from older crop-calendar routines. PyAEZ can support agricultural water-demand and production scenarios within food-supply simulations, complementing observed yields in CY-Bench (data-cy-bench-subnational-crop-yield-benchmark). The repository explains its six-module organisation and installation dependencies. Suitability is not an observed yield forecast. No climate grids, soil layers or parameter workbooks were downloaded.
